## Effect of riot exposure on names {#effects}

```{=latex}
\begin{econtable}{6.8}{7.8}
\input{tables/effects.tex}
\econnotes{Outcome: name index of the cohort born in t+1; higher values mean more distinctive names. Riot exposure is exp(−d²/(2·200²)), where d is the distance in km to the nearest district with a riot that year; Panel C instruments it with the Friday festival (Iyer and Shrivastava 2018). Controls: BJP rule, Muslim share, urbanisation, literacy, electricity and tap water. Standard errors clustered by district in parentheses; the appendix adds standard errors clustered by state-year. With one instrument, the reduced-form test is the Anderson–Rubin test of a zero effect, which stays valid when the instrument is weak. \stars{***}{0.01}, \stars{**}{0.05}, \stars{*}{0.1}.}
\end{econtable}
```

# Appendix {#appendix}

## Summary statistics {#summary-stats}

```{=latex}
\begin{econtable}{7.4}{8.8}
\input{tables/summary_stats.tex}
\econnotes{Name indices are the mean name score of the cohort born in t+1, with names scored on births before 1970; higher values mean more distinctive names, and the Hindu index is one minus the score. Numbers of Muslims and Hindus count voters in polling-booth cells with a scored name. Riot rows cover districts on the 1981 list, the only ones with own-district riot data; missing deaths and injuries count as 0. Riot exposure is exp(−d²/(2·200²)), where d is the distance in km to the nearest district with a riot that year.}
\end{econtable}
```

## Riot and non-riot district-years {#riot-comparison}

```{=latex}
\begin{econtable}{8}{9.6}
\input{tables/riot_comparison.tex}
\econnotes{District-years of the districts on the 1981 list, the only ones with own-district riot data. Difference: coefficient on riot in a regression of the row variable on riot, with standard errors clustered by district. \stars{***}{0.01}, \stars{**}{0.05}, \stars{*}{0.1}.}
\end{econtable}
```

## First stage by specification {#app-first-stage}

```{=latex}
\begin{econtable}{7}{8.4}
\input{tables/app_first_stage.tex}
\econnotes{Riot: a riot in the district, for districts on the 1981 list (0 elsewhere). Exposure: exp(−d²/(2·200²)), where d is the distance in km to the nearest district with a riot that year. Count: riots in the riot-data districts, weighted the same way. The instrument is 1 if one of the state's three main Hindu festivals, Dushehra or Diwali falls on a Friday, in the coding of Goyal and van Noort (2025) or of Iyer and Shrivastava (2018). Controls: BJP rule, Muslim share, urbanisation, literacy, electricity and tap water. Column 3 is the main specification. Standard errors clustered by district in parentheses and by state-year in brackets; stars use district clusters. \stars{***}{0.01}, \stars{**}{0.05}, \stars{*}{0.1}.}
\end{econtable}
```

## Anderson–Rubin tests by specification {#app-anderson-rubin}

```{=latex}
\begin{econtable}{6.6}{7.8}
\input{tables/app_anderson_rubin.tex}
\econnotes{The Anderson–Rubin (AR) test of a zero IV effect is the reduced-form t-test on the Friday festival; the AR 95\% set collects the IV effects that the test does not reject. Both stay valid when the instrument is weak, unlike the 2SLS standard errors. Columns as in the first stage by specification; column 3 is the main specification.}
\end{econtable}
```
